title: SLO Monitor Coverage Audit (Auto-rollback readiness) — Hosted/Dedicated/Private
content:
Last reviewed window: 2026-02-26 16:00–18:00 PT
Owner (sheet): Aisha Bello (SLO dashboards & burn-rate alerts)
Primary reviewers: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Allison Grant (obs standards), Logan Wright (telemetry)

Purpose
Track SLO monitor coverage for rollout-scoped signals (latency/error/saturation) and flag which monitors are SAFE to use as auto-rollback inputs for rollout-controller.

SAFE criteria (for auto-rollback signals)
- Monitor is rollout-scoped at minimum: service/route + region + customer_tier. Prefer: + model_id + model_version.
- Burn-rate supports dual windows (fast/slow), and returns sample size + last datapoint timestamp.
- Data freshness: last datapoint age <= 180s (unless explicitly marked for low-traffic routes w/ different staleness threshold).
- Label/cardinality is within standards (no unbounded labels like request_id, prompt_id).
- Paging/notification routing exists OR explicitly non-paging for self-serve routes.

NOT SAFE reasons (common)
- Missing monitor entirely (no SLO definition or no burn-rate endpoint coverage)
- Stale/misaligned time series (aggregation delay, missing labels, or “all-regions” only)
- Too-broad scope (service-level only; can’t isolate rollout step/model version)
- Low-volume routes without min-sample gating (false positives)
- Known instrumentation gaps during traffic shifting (A/B split labels missing)

Summary (rough counts; see table for details)
- SAFE: 14
- CONDITIONAL (safe w/ caveats): 9
- NOT SAFE: 11
Top blockers:
1) Missing model_version label on latency SLOs for hosted chat routes in eu-west
2) Saturation signals inconsistent across Dedicated GPU pools (capacity label mismatch)
3) Staleness detection not configured for 3 routes (burn-rate endpoint returns status but no datapoint timestamp)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Notes / Decisions needed
1) Stale monitor handling: current recommendation is “suppress auto action and emit monitor_stale outcome metric + Slack notify” (aligning with postmortem 2026-02-17). Needs final decision in controller policy semantics.
2) Private/on-prem: many installations won’t have full burn-rate support w/ timestamps. For MVP, recommend feature gated OFF by default for on-prem; VPC can be opt-in w/ PAUSE-only.
3) Saturation: unclear if saturation should trigger rollback in MVP. Recommend ‘signal eligible but default disabled’ until Dedicated pool label alignment is fixed.

Enablement readiness checklist (per service/route/region/tier)
- Latency SLO present and rollout-scoped (prefer model_version) AND fresh
- Error-rate SLO present and rollout-scoped AND fresh
- Staleness alert exists and routes to correct channel
- Burn-rate endpoint returns: status, burn_rate, sample_size, last_datapoint_ts
- Dashboard panel exists: “rollout SLO eval outcomes” + “auto action timeline”

Next update cadence
- Update weekly through launch hardening; after launch, update on monitor changes or new regions/routes.
- Please leave comments by @Aisha Bello and tag owners for new gaps.
